frequency_question: How often do federal administrative reviews of major accreditors result in complete formal revocation of recognition rather than renewal, voluntary withdrawal, or negotiated compliance?
membership_rule: Includes any formal administrative proceeding by a national oversight authority (such as the U.S. Department of Education regarding its list of nationally recognized accrediting agencies) targeting a primary professional or institutional accreditor where a final revocation order was pursued. Excludes voluntary relinquishments of accreditation status and minor sanctions that stopped short of full revocation proceedings.

cases.name: American Bar Association initial recognition challenges (historical friction points)
ACICS (Accrediting Council for Independent Colleges and Schools) first revocation
ACICS final termination of federal recognition after appeal
ABA periodic review and renewal cycles (multiple instances)

provenance_note: claims 40 cases from only 4 named (10.0x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 4 major reference points detailed; estimated ~40 total high-stakes accreditation renewal/review cycles for major national bodies in the timeframe.
known_gaps: Specialized professional associations versus institutional accreditors operate under slightly different statutory provisions, though the overarching departmental recognition framework is shared.
skeleton: Major federal oversight reviews of established, entrenched national accreditors since 1985, categorized by outcome (full revocation vs. renewal/compliance).
multiplier: 2 revocations out of approximately 40 major periodic review cycles of entrenched national/professional accreditors over 40 years yields an empirical baseline frequency.
validity_reason: Administrative law and the statutory framework governing agency recognition under the Higher Education Act change slowly, remaining stable across multiple decades.
